investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T11:05–11:06Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when the eval runner issued POST /api/agents. Because the failure occurred before any agent was created, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" on every attempt. This caused the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) to fail immediately, preventing any evidence from being written and causing all three sibling checks to fail with the same error. The root cause is localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer, not to the eval runner code itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval observability layer.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The AWS ELB in us-east-2 serving the swarm /v1/agents endpoint was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api gateway to return 502.

The production-api layer's internal HTTP client could not establish a connection to the ELB (DNS resolution failure, security group change, or VPC routing issue), resulting in the 'error sending request' message.
A deployment or infrastructure change to the swarm service or its ELB target group removed all healthy instances, causing the load balancer to return 502 with no upstream to forward to.
Transient network partition or AWS regional event in us-east-2 affecting the ELB at the moment of the eval run (would be self-healing; a re-run would confirm or rule this out).

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=634, max=300)
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 634 minutes old, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all three sibling public-website checks passed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 634 minutes. The expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) asserts snapshotAgeMinutes must be <= 300. The observed value of 634 violates that assertion by 334 minutes, indicating the snapshot-publishing workflow has been absent or failing for over 10 hours. The check is marked required=false with statusImpact=informational in the feature registry (infra/evals/status/features.json, line 383), so this does not constitute a product outage, but the snapshot data served to /observability is stale.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 634' — the single violated assertion that caused the eval to fail.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=634, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was generated by GitHub Actions but is 334 minutes past the freshness threshold.
expected-output.contract: infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 asserts { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } — the contract boundary that was crossed.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check is registered as required=false, statusImpact=informational, staleAfterMinutes=360 — confirms this is an informational eval failure, not a required-check outage.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses — the public website itself is reachable; the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from statusSnapshotEvidence(payload) — the age value is computed from the live payload, not a cached eval artifact.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot has not completed a successful run in over 634 minutes — it may have been skipped, cancelled, failed silently, or its schedule was disrupted.
The workflow ran but failed to push the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages branch, leaving the stale file in place while the workflow itself reports success.
A GitHub Actions quota, rate limit, or runner availability issue prevented the scheduled workflow from executing during the affected window.
The workflow schedule (cron) was inadvertently disabled or modified, causing it to stop triggering automatically.
The snapshot-publishing step within the workflow succeeded but the GitHub Pages deployment step failed or was skipped, so the published file was not updated.
